key_insight: Raman and EXAFS data show that SrLaCoNbO6 has strong spin-lattice coupling with anomalous phonon and local-structure changes well above its magnetic ordering temperature, consistent with fluctuating Kitaev-like interactions.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight how local lattice distortions and magnetic excitations can be probed to understand and potentially tune functional responses in ordered double perovskites.
method: Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy from high to low temperatures
Co K-edge EXAFS to track local bond distances and disorder
Line-shape analysis of phonons, including Fano asymmetry and continuum features
evidence_signal: Anomalies in phonon frequency, linewidth, intensity, and EXAFS bond metrics appear near 60 K and 160–180 K, above the antiferromagnetic transition at about 15 K.
watch_item: The observed anomalies suggest spin-lattice coupling, but a purely structural origin cannot be fully ruled out from the presented data alone.
paper_title: Raman spectroscopic signature of Kitaev magnetism and complex spin-lattice coupling in S = 1/2 antiferromagnet SrLaCoNbO$_6$ double perovskite
